E1 · Interpersonal cooperation (laborers)

Class 1 · Directly tests one of Hypotheses 1–4 in the main laborer sample.

Experiment design: factorial experiment; survey experiment

CategoryCriteria met / applicableN/A
Experimental design0/50
Statistical methods2/80
Results1/50
Validity1/20
Design map

Target population

Poor, predominantly male circular migrant construction workers using informal labor markets in Delhi and Lucknow.
“four vignette experiments embedded within a survey ... (N = 3,018)”PDF page 5 · Research Design; Vignette Experiment Design

The article identifies four laborer survey-vignette experiments and says ethnicity is manipulated through the hypothetical person’s name.

“3,018 migrant workers (1,818 in Delhi; 1,200 in Lucknow) ... across 58 chowks”PDF page 6 · Survey Implementation

The laborer survey total and city/market distribution are reported, but within-market recruitment and focal-analysis Ns are not.

Eligibility criteria

NR: construction-sector/circular-migrant focus and male sample are stated, but operational screening and inclusion criteria are not.
PDF page 5 · Main article methods/results and relevant figure notes

Operational eligibility/screening rules are absent from pp. 912–916; survey-protocol details are deferred to SI Supplement G.

Recruitment procedure

Markets were randomly sampled from an enumerated frame; NR for selection/recruitment of workers inside markets.
“labor markets randomly sampled from this list”PDF page 6 · Survey Implementation

Markets were randomly sampled from an enumerated list; respondent selection details are deferred to SI Supplement G.

Field dates and setting

Delhi and Lucknow chowks; survey dates NR. Ethnography occurred Sep–Nov 2013 (Delhi) and Feb 2014 (Lucknow).
“September to November 2013 in Delhi, and in February 2014 in Lucknow”PDF page 6 · Constructing Vignettes through Ethnography

These dates describe vignette-building ethnography, not survey administration; survey field dates are NR.

Number recruited and analyzed

3,018 interviewed (1,818 Delhi; 1,200 Lucknow) across 58 chowks; experiment-specific analyzed N NR.
“3,018 migrant workers (1,818 in Delhi; 1,200 in Lucknow) ... across 58 chowks”PDF page 6 · Survey Implementation

The laborer survey total and city/market distribution are reported, but within-market recruitment and focal-analysis Ns are not.

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Four possible names generated narrow-jati and broad-caste coethnic/non-coethnic contrasts; region of origin also varied.
“could receive any one of four different names in a vignette”PDF page 5 · Vignette Experiment Design

Four names induce respondent–target ethnic match or mismatch at narrow jati and broad caste levels; the names themselves are only in excluded SI.

“vignettes also varied a migrant’s region of origin”PDF page 11 · footnote 28

Region of origin was another randomized attribute, but its levels and assignment are not described in the main article.

Unit of randomization

Respondent/vignette presentation (a respondent received a hypothetical-person name); exact assignment implementation NR.
“could receive any one of four different names in a vignette”PDF page 5 · Vignette Experiment Design

Four names induce respondent–target ethnic match or mismatch at narrow jati and broad caste levels; the names themselves are only in excluded SI.

Allocation probabilities and restrictions

NR. The article gives four names and says no name repeated within respondent, but gives no probabilities or stratification.
“vignette questions were randomized across four fixed places”PDF page 5 · footnote 6

Question order was randomized; the paper does not state assignment probabilities, stratification, or restrictions for names.

Exact treatment and comparator

Non-coethnic hypothetical person versus coethnic hypothetical person at narrow and broad levels; exact names and full vignette text are outside the main article.
“could receive any one of four different names in a vignette”PDF page 5 · Vignette Experiment Design

Four names induce respondent–target ethnic match or mismatch at narrow jati and broad caste levels; the names themselves are only in excluded SI.

PDF page 5 · Main article methods/results and relevant figure notes

Full vignette wording and the name list are absent; pp. 912–915 point to SI Supplement A/A3.

Outcome definitions and timing

Would share a rented room with the hypothetical migrant, measured immediately after the vignette. Exact response options, coding transformation, and elapsed timing are NR.
“always scaled between 0 and 1”PDF page 8 · Main Results

The focal evaluation outcome is described and scaled 0–1, but the response categories and recoding are absent.

PDF page 7 · Outcome subsection

Exact response options and administration timing are absent from pp. 914–916.

Estimand

ATE of ethnic difference: average evaluation under non-coethnic rather than coethnic target, separately for narrow and broad ethnicity.
“Vertical lines indicate 95% confidence intervals.”PDF page 10 · Figure 1 and note

Figure 1 maps narrow and broad ethnic-difference ATEs to each laborer outcome and plots 95% CIs; the text reports exact effects and p-values.

Estimator or statistical model

OLS of 0–1 evaluation on non-coethnic indicator, market fixed effects and unnamed standard demographic controls.
“Average treatment effects are derived from ordinary least squares (OLS) regressions”PDF page 8 · Main Results continuing on p. 916

The outcome is scaled 0–1, treatment is non-coethnic=1 versus coethnic=0, and the model uses market fixed effects, unnamed demographic controls, and market-clustered SEs.

“market fixed effects ... standard demographic controls ... clustering by market”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Fixed effects and clustering level are reported, but demographic covariates are unnamed and CI construction is not stated.

Analysis unit

Individual survey respondent’s evaluation in this vignette.
“Average treatment effects are derived from ordinary least squares (OLS) regressions”PDF page 8 · Main Results continuing on p. 916

The outcome is scaled 0–1, treatment is non-coethnic=1 versus coethnic=0, and the model uses market fixed effects, unnamed demographic controls, and market-clustered SEs.

Variable coding and reference categories

Treatment 1=non-coethnic, 0=coethnic; outcome scaled 0–1 but exact response coding NR; coethnic is reference.
“coded 1 when ... different ethnic groups, and 0 otherwise”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Treatment and reference coding are explicit; the original response options and exact 0–1 outcome recoding are not.

Covariates and fixed effects

Market fixed effects and “standard demographic controls”; covariate names, weights, and exact transformations NR.
“market fixed effects ... standard demographic controls ... clustering by market”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Fixed effects and clustering level are reported, but demographic covariates are unnamed and CI construction is not stated.

Standard-error and inference procedure

SEs clustered by market; Figure 1 shows 95% CIs and text p-values. Exact CI and p-value construction NR.
“Vertical lines indicate 95% confidence intervals.”PDF page 10 · Figure 1 and note

Figure 1 maps narrow and broad ethnic-difference ATEs to each laborer outcome and plots 95% CIs; the text reports exact effects and p-values.

“market fixed effects ... standard demographic controls ... clustering by market”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Fixed effects and clustering level are reported, but demographic covariates are unnamed and CI construction is not stated.

Handling of clustering or repeated observations

Market-clustered SEs; no explanation of cross-vignette repeated observations, though each outcome is analyzed in its own vignette model.
“market fixed effects ... standard demographic controls ... clustering by market”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Fixed effects and clustering level are reported, but demographic covariates are unnamed and CI construction is not stated.

Missing-data and attrition rules

NR.
PDF page 5 · Main article methods/results and relevant figure notes

No missing-outcome, item-nonresponse, attrition, or adjustment rule appears on pp. 912–921.

Effect estimates and uncertainty

-0.104 narrow-jati ATE and -0.127 broad-caste ATE; both p<.001; Figure 1 gives 95% CIs.
“Vertical lines indicate 95% confidence intervals.”PDF page 10 · Figure 1 and note

Figure 1 maps narrow and broad ethnic-difference ATEs to each laborer outcome and plots 95% CIs; the text reports exact effects and p-values.

PDF page 7 · Main Results and Figure 1

-0.104 narrow-jati ATE and -0.127 broad-caste ATE; both p<.001; Figure 1 gives 95% CIs.

Target population

Poor, predominantly male circular migrant construction workers using informal labor markets in Delhi and Lucknow.
“four vignette experiments embedded within a survey ... (N = 3,018)”PDF page 5 · Research Design; Vignette Experiment Design

The article identifies four laborer survey-vignette experiments and says ethnicity is manipulated through the hypothetical person’s name.

“3,018 migrant workers (1,818 in Delhi; 1,200 in Lucknow) ... across 58 chowks”PDF page 6 · Survey Implementation

The laborer survey total and city/market distribution are reported, but within-market recruitment and focal-analysis Ns are not.

Eligibility criteria

NR: construction-sector/circular-migrant focus and male sample are stated, but operational screening and inclusion criteria are not.
PDF page 5 · Main article methods/results and relevant figure notes

Operational eligibility/screening rules are absent from pp. 912–916; survey-protocol details are deferred to SI Supplement G.

Recruitment procedure

Markets were randomly sampled from an enumerated frame; NR for selection/recruitment of workers inside markets.
“labor markets randomly sampled from this list”PDF page 6 · Survey Implementation

Markets were randomly sampled from an enumerated list; respondent selection details are deferred to SI Supplement G.

Field dates and setting

Delhi and Lucknow chowks; survey dates NR. Ethnography occurred Sep–Nov 2013 (Delhi) and Feb 2014 (Lucknow).
“September to November 2013 in Delhi, and in February 2014 in Lucknow”PDF page 6 · Constructing Vignettes through Ethnography

These dates describe vignette-building ethnography, not survey administration; survey field dates are NR.

Number recruited and analyzed

3,018 interviewed (1,818 Delhi; 1,200 Lucknow) across 58 chowks; experiment-specific analyzed N NR.
“3,018 migrant workers (1,818 in Delhi; 1,200 in Lucknow) ... across 58 chowks”PDF page 6 · Survey Implementation

The laborer survey total and city/market distribution are reported, but within-market recruitment and focal-analysis Ns are not.

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Four possible names generated narrow-jati and broad-caste coethnic/non-coethnic contrasts; region of origin also varied.
“could receive any one of four different names in a vignette”PDF page 5 · Vignette Experiment Design

Four names induce respondent–target ethnic match or mismatch at narrow jati and broad caste levels; the names themselves are only in excluded SI.

“vignettes also varied a migrant’s region of origin”PDF page 11 · footnote 28

Region of origin was another randomized attribute, but its levels and assignment are not described in the main article.

Unit of randomization

Respondent/vignette presentation (a respondent received a hypothetical-person name); exact assignment implementation NR.
“could receive any one of four different names in a vignette”PDF page 5 · Vignette Experiment Design

Four names induce respondent–target ethnic match or mismatch at narrow jati and broad caste levels; the names themselves are only in excluded SI.

Allocation probabilities and restrictions

NR. The article gives four names and says no name repeated within respondent, but gives no probabilities or stratification.
“vignette questions were randomized across four fixed places”PDF page 5 · footnote 6

Question order was randomized; the paper does not state assignment probabilities, stratification, or restrictions for names.

Exact treatment and comparator

Non-coethnic hypothetical person versus coethnic hypothetical person at narrow and broad levels; exact names and full vignette text are outside the main article.
“could receive any one of four different names in a vignette”PDF page 5 · Vignette Experiment Design

Four names induce respondent–target ethnic match or mismatch at narrow jati and broad caste levels; the names themselves are only in excluded SI.

PDF page 5 · Main article methods/results and relevant figure notes

Full vignette wording and the name list are absent; pp. 912–915 point to SI Supplement A/A3.

Outcome definitions and timing

Whether laborers like the wage-cutting hypothetical migrant constitute an economic threat, measured immediately after the vignette. Exact response options, coding transformation, and elapsed timing are NR.
“always scaled between 0 and 1”PDF page 8 · Main Results

The focal evaluation outcome is described and scaled 0–1, but the response categories and recoding are absent.

PDF page 7 · Outcome subsection

Exact response options and administration timing are absent from pp. 914–916.

Estimand

ATE of ethnic difference: average evaluation under non-coethnic rather than coethnic target, separately for narrow and broad ethnicity.
“Vertical lines indicate 95% confidence intervals.”PDF page 10 · Figure 1 and note

Figure 1 maps narrow and broad ethnic-difference ATEs to each laborer outcome and plots 95% CIs; the text reports exact effects and p-values.

Estimator or statistical model

OLS of 0–1 evaluation on non-coethnic indicator, market fixed effects and unnamed standard demographic controls.
“Average treatment effects are derived from ordinary least squares (OLS) regressions”PDF page 8 · Main Results continuing on p. 916

The outcome is scaled 0–1, treatment is non-coethnic=1 versus coethnic=0, and the model uses market fixed effects, unnamed demographic controls, and market-clustered SEs.

“market fixed effects ... standard demographic controls ... clustering by market”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Fixed effects and clustering level are reported, but demographic covariates are unnamed and CI construction is not stated.

Analysis unit

Individual survey respondent’s evaluation in this vignette.
“Average treatment effects are derived from ordinary least squares (OLS) regressions”PDF page 8 · Main Results continuing on p. 916

The outcome is scaled 0–1, treatment is non-coethnic=1 versus coethnic=0, and the model uses market fixed effects, unnamed demographic controls, and market-clustered SEs.

Variable coding and reference categories

Treatment 1=non-coethnic, 0=coethnic; outcome scaled 0–1 but exact response coding NR; coethnic is reference.
“coded 1 when ... different ethnic groups, and 0 otherwise”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Treatment and reference coding are explicit; the original response options and exact 0–1 outcome recoding are not.

Covariates and fixed effects

Market fixed effects and “standard demographic controls”; covariate names, weights, and exact transformations NR.
“market fixed effects ... standard demographic controls ... clustering by market”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Fixed effects and clustering level are reported, but demographic covariates are unnamed and CI construction is not stated.

Standard-error and inference procedure

SEs clustered by market; Figure 1 shows 95% CIs and text p-values. Exact CI and p-value construction NR.
“Vertical lines indicate 95% confidence intervals.”PDF page 10 · Figure 1 and note

Figure 1 maps narrow and broad ethnic-difference ATEs to each laborer outcome and plots 95% CIs; the text reports exact effects and p-values.

“market fixed effects ... standard demographic controls ... clustering by market”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Fixed effects and clustering level are reported, but demographic covariates are unnamed and CI construction is not stated.

Handling of clustering or repeated observations

Market-clustered SEs; no explanation of cross-vignette repeated observations, though each outcome is analyzed in its own vignette model.
“market fixed effects ... standard demographic controls ... clustering by market”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Fixed effects and clustering level are reported, but demographic covariates are unnamed and CI construction is not stated.

Missing-data and attrition rules

NR.
PDF page 5 · Main article methods/results and relevant figure notes

No missing-outcome, item-nonresponse, attrition, or adjustment rule appears on pp. 912–921.

Effect estimates and uncertainty

-0.020 narrow-jati ATE (p=.443) and -0.023 broad-caste ATE (p=.126); Figure 1 gives 95% CIs.
“Vertical lines indicate 95% confidence intervals.”PDF page 10 · Figure 1 and note

Figure 1 maps narrow and broad ethnic-difference ATEs to each laborer outcome and plots 95% CIs; the text reports exact effects and p-values.

PDF page 7 · Main Results and Figure 1

-0.020 narrow-jati ATE (p=.443) and -0.023 broad-caste ATE (p=.126); Figure 1 gives 95% CIs.

Class 1 · Directly tests one of Hypotheses 1–4 in the main laborer sample.

Experiment design: factorial experiment; survey experiment

CategoryCriteria met / applicableN/A

Validity1/20
Design map

Target population

Poor, predominantly male circular migrant construction workers using informal labor markets in Delhi and Lucknow.
“four vignette experiments embedded within a survey ... (N = 3,018)”PDF page 5 · Research Design; Vignette Experiment Design

The article identifies four laborer survey-vignette experiments and says ethnicity is manipulated through the hypothetical person’s name.

“3,018 migrant workers (1,818 in Delhi; 1,200 in Lucknow) ... across 58 chowks”PDF page 6 · Survey Implementation

The laborer survey total and city/market distribution are reported, but within-market recruitment and focal-analysis Ns are not.

Eligibility criteria

NR: construction-sector/circular-migrant focus and male sample are stated, but operational screening and inclusion criteria are not.
PDF page 5 · Main article methods/results and relevant figure notes

Operational eligibility/screening rules are absent from pp. 912–916; survey-protocol details are deferred to SI Supplement G.

Recruitment procedure

Markets were randomly sampled from an enumerated frame; NR for selection/recruitment of workers inside markets.
“labor markets randomly sampled from this list”PDF page 6 · Survey Implementation

Markets were randomly sampled from an enumerated list; respondent selection details are deferred to SI Supplement G.

Field dates and setting

Delhi and Lucknow chowks; survey dates NR. Ethnography occurred Sep–Nov 2013 (Delhi) and Feb 2014 (Lucknow).
“September to November 2013 in Delhi, and in February 2014 in Lucknow”PDF page 6 · Constructing Vignettes through Ethnography

These dates describe vignette-building ethnography, not survey administration; survey field dates are NR.

Number recruited and analyzed

3,018 interviewed (1,818 Delhi; 1,200 Lucknow) across 58 chowks; experiment-specific analyzed N NR.
“3,018 migrant workers (1,818 in Delhi; 1,200 in Lucknow) ... across 58 chowks”PDF page 6 · Survey Implementation

The laborer survey total and city/market distribution are reported, but within-market recruitment and focal-analysis Ns are not.

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Four possible names generated narrow-jati and broad-caste coethnic/non-coethnic contrasts; region of origin also varied. Candidate constituency (urban/rural) and party also varied.
“could receive any one of four different names in a vignette”PDF page 5 · Vignette Experiment Design

Four names induce respondent–target ethnic match or mismatch at narrow jati and broad caste levels; the names themselves are only in excluded SI.

“vignettes also varied a migrant’s region of origin”PDF page 11 · footnote 28

Region of origin was another randomized attribute, but its levels and assignment are not described in the main article.

Unit of randomization

Respondent/vignette presentation (a respondent received a hypothetical-person name); exact assignment implementation NR.
“could receive any one of four different names in a vignette”PDF page 5 · Vignette Experiment Design

Four names induce respondent–target ethnic match or mismatch at narrow jati and broad caste levels; the names themselves are only in excluded SI.

Allocation probabilities and restrictions

NR. The article gives four names and says no name repeated within respondent, but gives no probabilities or stratification.
“vignette questions were randomized across four fixed places”PDF page 5 · footnote 6

Question order was randomized; the paper does not state assignment probabilities, stratification, or restrictions for names.

Exact treatment and comparator

Non-coethnic hypothetical person versus coethnic hypothetical person at narrow and broad levels; exact names and full vignette text are outside the main article.
“could receive any one of four different names in a vignette”PDF page 5 · Vignette Experiment Design

Four names induce respondent–target ethnic match or mismatch at narrow jati and broad caste levels; the names themselves are only in excluded SI.

PDF page 5 · Main article methods/results and relevant figure notes

Full vignette wording and the name list are absent; pp. 912–915 point to SI Supplement A/A3.

Outcome definitions and timing

Would support the hypothetical state-assembly candidate in an election, measured after the speech vignette. Exact response options, coding transformation, and elapsed timing are NR.
“always scaled between 0 and 1”PDF page 8 · Main Results

The focal evaluation outcome is described and scaled 0–1, but the response categories and recoding are absent.

PDF page 8 · Outcome subsection

Exact response options and administration timing are absent from pp. 914–916.

Estimand

ATE of ethnic difference: average evaluation under non-coethnic rather than coethnic target, separately for narrow and broad ethnicity.
“Vertical lines indicate 95% confidence intervals.”PDF page 10 · Figure 1 and note

Figure 1 maps narrow and broad ethnic-difference ATEs to each laborer outcome and plots 95% CIs; the text reports exact effects and p-values.

Estimator or statistical model

OLS of 0–1 evaluation on non-coethnic indicator, market fixed effects and unnamed standard demographic controls.
“Average treatment effects are derived from ordinary least squares (OLS) regressions”PDF page 8 · Main Results continuing on p. 916

The outcome is scaled 0–1, treatment is non-coethnic=1 versus coethnic=0, and the model uses market fixed effects, unnamed demographic controls, and market-clustered SEs.

“market fixed effects ... standard demographic controls ... clustering by market”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Fixed effects and clustering level are reported, but demographic covariates are unnamed and CI construction is not stated.

Analysis unit

Individual survey respondent’s evaluation in this vignette.
“Average treatment effects are derived from ordinary least squares (OLS) regressions”PDF page 8 · Main Results continuing on p. 916

The outcome is scaled 0–1, treatment is non-coethnic=1 versus coethnic=0, and the model uses market fixed effects, unnamed demographic controls, and market-clustered SEs.

Variable coding and reference categories

Treatment 1=non-coethnic, 0=coethnic; outcome scaled 0–1 but exact response coding NR; coethnic is reference.
“coded 1 when ... different ethnic groups, and 0 otherwise”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Treatment and reference coding are explicit; the original response options and exact 0–1 outcome recoding are not.

Covariates and fixed effects

Market fixed effects and “standard demographic controls”; covariate names, weights, and exact transformations NR.
“market fixed effects ... standard demographic controls ... clustering by market”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Fixed effects and clustering level are reported, but demographic covariates are unnamed and CI construction is not stated.

Standard-error and inference procedure

SEs clustered by market; Figure 1 shows 95% CIs and text p-values. Exact CI and p-value construction NR.
“Vertical lines indicate 95% confidence intervals.”PDF page 10 · Figure 1 and note

Figure 1 maps narrow and broad ethnic-difference ATEs to each laborer outcome and plots 95% CIs; the text reports exact effects and p-values.

“market fixed effects ... standard demographic controls ... clustering by market”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Fixed effects and clustering level are reported, but demographic covariates are unnamed and CI construction is not stated.

Handling of clustering or repeated observations

Market-clustered SEs; no explanation of cross-vignette repeated observations, though each outcome is analyzed in its own vignette model.
“market fixed effects ... standard demographic controls ... clustering by market”PDF page 9 · Main Results

Fixed effects and clustering level are reported, but demographic covariates are unnamed and CI construction is not stated.

Missing-data and attrition rules

NR except eight respondents excluded from the formal-politics analysis for constituency exposure.
“Such respondents were excluded (N = 8).”PDF page 8 · footnote 15

Formal-politics exclusions are reported, but missing-outcome and attrition rules remain NR.

Effect estimates and uncertainty

Urban-candidate ethnic ATEs: about -0.001 narrow jati (p=.870) and -0.020 broad caste (p=.321), with 95% CIs. Rural-candidate results are described as significant but their estimates and uncertainty are only in excluded SI Figure S.1.
“Vertical lines indicate 95% confidence intervals.”PDF page 10 · Figure 1 and note

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Four possible names generated narrow-jati and broad-caste coethnic/non-coethnic contrasts; region of origin also varied.
